definition: A huge ball of hot gas, held together by its own gravity, that gives out light and other electromagnetic radiation; nuclear reactions in its centre release the energy. The Sun is a medium-sized star.

A star in the long, steady main stage of its life, such as the Sun now: the inward pull of gravity is balanced by an outward force caused by the very high temperature at its centre, and hydrogen nuclei fuse into helium in its core.
